tasks.short: Set regulatory priorities and the budget.

steps.what: Sum open submissions and the hours already logged.
Establish regulatory priorities, budgets, and workloads.
Record the budget and the resources the manager allocated.

tasks.design: Open submissions and logged hours are summed from {PROJECT} and the {ERP}. The regulatory affairs manager sets priorities, the budget, and the workload. The summary does not name who should do the work and does not score anyone. A submission with no hour record stays out of the sum.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workload was a feeling in the weekly meeting, and the budget was copied from last year.
tasks.enabler_now: Hours already logged against a submission can be summed before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Work that has not started, and a priority the numbers do not show.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can put a small file first because the agency date is immovable.
tasks.altitude: The numbers are ready. The allocation stays with the manager. Nobody is rostered or scored from this task.

reach.task: Read hours on a project before setting the budget, and do not rank the people.
reach.learn: The sum can be prepared. The priority is still a decision.

evidence.claim: A project file can sum hours already logged. It cannot set the budget or rank staff.

EU AI Act Annex III 4(a) and 4(b) cover hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits, with duties from 2 December 2027. This task stores no skill score and no named roster. Works-council consent applies before a new store of who attended.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Submission id and logged hours, produced by the project file. A submission with no hours is shown as unknown, not as zero priority. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the project and finance records the company already keeps. No new staff score is stored.
unknowns: Who else approves the regulatory budget.
research_questions: Are hours logged against the submission or only against a cost centre?
Which priorities last year were not the largest files?

already_counted.description: The manager still sets the allocation.
The manager still records the budget.

incremental.description: The manager corrects a submission whose hours were logged to the wrong file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the sum of hours already logged. It disappears when hours are missing and the manager rebuilds the picture. The allocation itself stays, so the net stays under the prior.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open the policy version the session will teach.
Train staff in the regulatory policies and procedures.
Record attendance without a skill score.

tasks.design: The signed policy version is opened from {DOCS} for the session. The regulatory affairs manager trains the staff. Attendance may be stored in the {LMS} only after works-council consent, and it stores no skill score. The screen does not certify that someone understood the policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training used whatever copy was to hand, and attendance was a paper sheet in a drawer.
tasks.enabler_now: The signed version can be the pack, and attendance can be a list if consent exists.
tasks.still_hard: A question the policy does not answer, and a person who attended and did not understand.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell a quiet room from a room that has understood the rule.
tasks.altitude: Teaching stays with the manager. Attendance is a list, not a score. No one is marked competent by the screen.

reach.task: Teach a signed procedure and keep competence as a person's judgement.
reach.learn: The pack can be the signed version. The teaching cannot be a quiz score.

evidence.claim: A learning record can store who attended a named session. It cannot score understanding.

EU AI Act Annex III 4(a) and 4(b) cover hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits, with duties from 2 December 2027. This task stores no skill score and no named roster. Works-council consent applies before a new store of who attended.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Policy version and session id, produced by the policy register. A session with no version id is not opened from the register. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the learning record the company already keeps, and only if works-council consent covers attendance. No extra score field.
unknowns: Whether consent for an attendance list already exists.
Which roles must attend which policy.
research_questions: Which policies require a person to judge competence?

incremental.description: The manager updates the pack when the policy version changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is opening the signed policy. It disappears when consent for an attendance list is refused and the manager keeps a paper list. The teaching time is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open the procedure and its review date.
Draft the local working practice from the approved change.

loop.input: the procedure and the approved change
loop.check: every change cites the approved change
loop.stop: stop when a change cites nothing
loop.why_not_simpler: local practice is prose, and a fixed edit would add a step

steps.what: Approve the standard operating procedure text.

tasks.design: Procedures due for review are listed from {DOCS}. A draft of the local working practice may cite only an approved change. The regulatory affairs manager approves the standard operating procedure. Publishing uses that signed version. A change with no approval is not published.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local practices drifted in personal files, and the official procedure was years older.
tasks.enabler_now: A review date and an approved change can be the only inputs to a draft.
tasks.still_hard: A local practice that is real and has never been approved.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can refuse a local step that the approved change does not allow.

ambition.what: A procedure past its review date enters the queue the week it falls due, and the text still changes only when the manager signs it.

tasks.altitude: The queue shows what is due. The text is still approved by the manager. An unsigned local practice is not the procedure.

reach.task: Keep a review date on a procedure and publish only the signed version.
reach.learn: The date can be configured. The local practice is still approved here.

evidence.claim: A register can show a review date and hold a draft to an approved change. It cannot approve the procedure.

A drafted sentence may cite only a rule or a figure already in the file. A sentence with neither stops and the manager rewrites it. The signed version is the only one published. A local practice with no approval stays a draft.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Procedure id, review date, and approved change id, produced by the procedure register. A change with no id is not drafted. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the procedure register the company already keeps.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
A drafted sentence may cite only a rule or a figure already in the file. A sentence with neither stops and the manager rewrites it.
unknowns: Which sites may keep a local practice.
Who besides the manager must sign.
research_questions: What share of procedures are past their review date?
Which local practices have no approved change behind them?

already_counted.description: The manager still approves the text.

incremental.description: The manager rewrites a change that cited nothing.

approvals.approved_version: procedure version and the change ids the draft cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the due list and a draft tied to an approved change. It disappears when there is no approved change and the manager rewrites the procedure. The approval time remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Contribute to the business operating plan.

steps.what: Pull regulatory dates that the operating plan must see.
Write the regulatory contribution to the operating plan.
Check the contribution cites only those dates.

tasks.design: Regulatory dates already in {DOCS} are listed for the plan year. The regulatory affairs manager writes the contribution to the business unit's strategic and operating plans. A sentence that needs a date not on the list is unfinished. The list does not write the strategy.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan chapter was written from memory of agency dates, and a renewal was missed.
tasks.enabler_now: Dates already decided can be listed before the chapter is written.
tasks.still_hard: A strategic bet that is not a date, and a date that is not yet decided.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can say that a listed date still does not make the plan realistic.
tasks.altitude: The dates are listed. The contribution is still the manager's writing. Strategy is not generated.

reach.task: Put a dated commitment into a plan and leave the strategy sentence to the owner.
reach.learn: The dates can be listed. The plan sentence is still written here.

evidence.claim: A date list can be pulled from a register. It cannot write a strategic plan.

A drafted sentence may cite only a rule or a figure already in the file. A sentence with neither stops and the manager rewrites it. The contribution is the manager's text. A date that is not in the file is not inserted.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Plan year and regulatory date id, produced by the regulatory calendar. A year with no dates shows an empty list, not a generated plan. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the calendar the regulatory team already keeps.
unknowns: Which business unit owns the operating plan.
Which dates are confidential before announcement.
research_questions: Is the regulatory calendar complete for the plan year?
What share of the chapter is dates rather than strategy?

already_counted.description: The manager still writes the contribution.
The manager still checks the citations.

incremental.description: The manager adds a date the calendar missed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the date list. It disappears when the calendar is empty and the manager gathers dates by hand. The writing of the plan stays, so the net stays under the prior.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Dates and procedure versions can be listed. The manager still sets the budget, still trains people, and still writes the contribution to the operating plan.
reach: Compliance managers keep a procedure version and a review date, and publish only the signed text.
Architectural and engineering managers set a project budget from hours already logged, not from a score of people.
skills_to_grow: Set priorities from open submissions and hours, not from a ranking of staff.
Record attendance at training without storing a skill score.
role.ambitious_version: A procedure past its review date is in the queue the week it falls due, and the budget is still the manager's allocation.
